bangkok-art-and-culture-centre.title: The circular ramp crossing the escalators
bangkok-art-and-culture-centre.direction: Frame a wide view from a balcony where visitors may stand. Look down so the curves of each level wrap around the frame, then place the escalator as a diagonal through the centre. Coordinate with the art centre before setting up a camera or lights.

saphan-han.title: The curved canal edge and reflected lights
saphan-han.direction: Place the camera parallel to the canal-side walkway. Use the bridge rail as a middle-ground line and keep coloured light reflections in the lower half of the frame. Decorative lights may only be switched on at certain times.

khlong-ong-ang.title: The canal leading the eye between both rows of buildings
khlong-ong-ang.direction: Set up from a bridge rail where standing is allowed. Follow the canal and use the walkway edges on both sides to lead into the centre, with buildings and trees framing the view.

talat-noi.title: Shophouses and layered shop signs
talat-noi.direction: Look along the street from a public path. Layer shop signs and overhead wires at different distances for a tighter frame that still shows the building textures and background.

tham-krasae-railway-station.title: Repeating platform roofs beside the hillside
tham-krasae-railway-station.direction: Use a diagonal view from an authorised part of the platform. Follow the roofline with the hills behind the station to create depth while keeping the camera on the platform.

khao-ngu-stone-park.title: The mountain pass reflected in the water
khao-ngu-stone-park.direction: Place the gap between the two cliffs in the centre of the frame. Keep the waterline near the middle for a reflection, and try a slightly lower angle from an open walkway.

phae-mueang-phi.title: Earth pillars against the sky and vertical ground textures
phae-mueang-phi.direction: Use a low wide angle from the path. Let the largest earth pillar fill one side of the frame and leave negative space on the other. The reference light is specific to that moment; confirm access hours before scheduling a shoot.

bangkok-kunsthalle.title: Building levels converging above the alley
bangkok-kunsthalle.direction: Tilt up from outside so the levels on both sides converge toward the bright space in the centre. This works for an opening shot where the old buildings enclose the subject.

chao-phraya-sky-park.title: Curving rails and the city above the river
chao-phraya-sky-park.direction: Choose a diagonal view from the walkway. Let the rail and planter edges lead toward buildings on the opposite bank. Keep the subject to the inside so the path remains clear.

kudi-chin.title: Mural walls in a narrow lane
kudi-chin.direction: Frame diagonally along the wall so the murals form a leading line. Include a little of the walkway to show the true scale of the lane.

talat-phlu-railway-station.title: Shops on both sides framing the tracks
talat-phlu-railway-station.direction: Shoot from an authorised part of the platform. Use the eaves as a top frame and let the rails converge in the distance. A steady shot can hold both the tracks and the shopfront activity.

holy-rosary-church-bangkok.title: Arched ceiling bays above the nave
holy-rosary-church-bangkok.direction: If indoor photography is permitted, align the central aisle so each vaulted bay layers into the next. Include enough of the side windows to convey the height of the nave.

sampeng-market.title: A narrow aisle between fabrics and shop stalls
sampeng-market.direction: Use items hanging beside a shop as a near-camera frame, leaving a clear channel into the long aisle. Keep to the public walkway and avoid crowded periods if a tripod is needed.

pipit-banglamphu.title: A vivid archway and the gallery walkway
pipit-banglamphu.direction: Use the first room's arch as a foreground frame, then angle the view to include the colour in the next room and floor reflections. Coordinate with the venue before a production shoot.

ban-laem-railway-station.title: A red train framed by platform shadows
ban-laem-railway-station.direction: Shoot from an authorised part of the platform. Let the roof run diagonally and place the front of the train near the frame edge. The red stands out against the eaves' shadows when a train is present.

wat-yai-suwannaram.title: Temple walkway columns and eaves
wat-yai-suwannaram.direction: Stand at the edge of the walkway and angle the view so the white columns and layered eaves recede into the distance. Use the brick floor as a leading line.

kantang-railway-station.title: The yellow wooden hall and floor reflections
kantang-railway-station.direction: Use a low angle from an authorised walkway. Keep the posts and roof structure in the upper part of the frame, leaving room below for the warm wood tones to reflect.

thai-hua-museum.title: Windows and three entrance arches on the Sino-Portuguese building
thai-hua-museum.direction: Centre a wide view on the façade to include the upper windows and all three arches. Leave enough of the forecourt for a subject to stand in front.

chiang-mai-city-arts-and-cultural-centre.title: The historic façade and city square
chiang-mai-city-arts-and-cultural-centre.direction: Use a straight-on view from the square. Leave room for both wings and the central roofline; place the subject between the camera and building to show the scale.

river-city-bangkok.title: Blue glass panels and the riverfront line
river-city-bangkok.direction: Use a diagonal view from an accessible part of the riverfront. Let the long side of the building recede into the frame, with the water in the foreground. This reference emphasises the full building.

mae-fah-luang-art-and-cultural-park.title: A wooden pavilion reflected in the pond
mae-fah-luang-art-and-cultural-park.direction: Place the pavilion across the water. Use the trees to frame the left and right edges, leaving the lower half open so the roof reflection remains visible.

lanna-folklife-museum.title: The pale façade against the night scene
lanna-folklife-museum.direction: Use a centred view from the square and include both wings of the building. The reference uses the building's own lighting; ask the venue when those lights are on.

baan-dam-museum.title: Black-house rooflines and the sculpture in front
baan-dam-museum.direction: Use the sculpture as foreground and tilt up slightly so the pointed black roof cuts across the sky. Keep the roofline and carved door in the same frame, from an area where museum photography is allowed.

neilson-hays-library.title: The arched portico and library lettering
neilson-hays-library.direction: Photograph from outside under the library's rules. Let leaves at the side frame the arch, then tilt up to include the capitals and lettering along the curve.

sala-chalermkrung-royal-theatre.title: Sala Chalermkrung's corner rising into the sky
sala-chalermkrung-royal-theatre.direction: From a pavement with a view of two sides of the building, tilt up slightly so the corner leads toward the rooftop sign. Keep the window pattern of both wings in frame.

sanam-chai-mrt-station.title: Sanam Chai station's column hall from the centre axis
sanam-chai-mrt-station.direction: In areas open to passengers, use a floor seam to find the centre axis and let the two rows of columns lead beneath the red ceiling. Keep walkways clear and ask the operator before filming.

phitthayasathian-bridge.title: Phitthayasathian Bridge and the lit Chai Phatthanasin Building
phitthayasathian-bridge.direction: From an accessible riverside path, let the bridge rail cut in from the side toward the centre. Leave the opposite bank open to show the building's light reflected on the water.

khlong-phadung-krung-kasem.title: The steel framework of the canal bridge
khlong-phadung-krung-kasem.direction: From the canal edge, use a diagonal view so the curved steel rail rises from a lower corner. Choose a point where the gaps between posts and the water below are both visible.

wat-pariwat.title: Wat Pariwat's gold gable and decorated columns
wat-pariwat.direction: Use a diagonal view from a courtyard open to visitors. Let the front columns recede to the right and leave enough sky to include the full roof finials.

hua-takhe-railway-station.title: The platform eaves and potted plants at Hua Takhe Station
hua-takhe-railway-station.direction: From an authorised waiting area, keep the roof edge and platform edge as parallel diagonal lines. Use the pots as foreground and remain behind the safety line.
